subject: math

unit.title: Time to 5 minutes
unit.essentialQuestion: How do we read the clock to the nearest 5 minutes, and when do we say 'past' or 'to'?

title: Minutes to the hour
objectives: By the end, I can read 'minutes to' times once the minute hand passes the 6.

vocabulary.definition: how many minutes are LEFT before the next hour
15 minutes left before the next hour — minute hand on the 9
minute hand straight down on the 6 — halfway round
count the minutes remaining, from the minute hand up to the 12
the hour that's coming — the one we count TO
vocabulary.example: at twenty to 6, the next hour is 6

emphasize: Once the minute hand passes the 6 (half past), we switch to counting how many minutes are LEFT until the next hour — 'minutes to'.
Pre-empt the classic mistake: minute hand on the 8 is '20 to', NOT '40 past'.
At 'to' times the hour hand is nearly at the NEXT number — we name the hour we're counting TO.

keyConcepts: the clock's left side (6 round to 12) is the 'to' side
count the minutes remaining up to the 12 in 5s
quarter to = minute hand on the 9
misconceptions: carrying on counting up past the 6 — saying '40 past' instead of '20 to'
counting in the wrong direction (from the 12 down to the hand instead of the hand up to the 12)
naming the wrong hour: at twenty to 6 the hour hand sits between 5 and 6, so the child says 'twenty to 5'
hooks: Something funny happens after half past: we stop counting UP and start counting DOWN to the next hour — why?

digital: animated clock faces on the whiteboard block (with the past/to halves marked)

video.title: How to Tell Time to the Nearest 5 Minutes | Reading a Clock
video.watchTask: Every time the minute hand lands on the LEFT side of the clock, shout 'TO!' before Mr. J says the time.

afterCheck.question: When the minute hand was past the 6, what did we count — minutes gone by, or minutes left?
afterCheck.expectedAnswer: Minutes left until the next hour — that's why we say 'to'.

plan.goal: Spark curiosity about the switch at half past; retrieve 'past' and counting in 5s from Lesson 19.
plan.note: Don't explain yet — just make the switch feel like a mystery worth solving.
plan.successCriteria: Child says 'past' for the right side of the clock and counts 5, 10, 15, 20 without help.

script.say: Something funny happens after half past. We stop counting UP… and start counting DOWN to the next hour. Why would we do that? Let's find out! But first, a memory check: when the long minute hand was on the RIGHT side of the clock, what word did we use? … And count in 5s for me: 5, 10…
script.adaptHints: Listen for 'past' and a confident 5s count. If the 5s count is shaky, count round the right side of the clock together first — that skill carries the whole lesson.

stuckProtocol: If 'past' doesn't come back: point at the right side — 'minute hand here, we said 5 past, 10 past… what's the word?'
If counting in 5s is shaky: count round the clock numbers together — each number is worth 5.

plan.goal: Model the 'to' side: from 6 round to 12 we count the minutes LEFT until the next hour, in 5s from the hand up to the 12.
plan.note: Anchor phrase: 'Past the 6 → count the minutes LEFT → say ___ to.' Model minute hand on the 8 (20 to) and on the 9 (quarter to). Name the '40 past' trap out loud so it never traps them.
plan.successCriteria: Child hears the rule and echoes 'count what's left' for a hand on the left side.

script.say: Here's the secret. The LEFT side of the clock, from the 6 round to the 12, is the 'TO' side. There, we count how many minutes are LEFT until the next hour. Watch: the minute hand is on the 8. I count from the 8 up to the 12 — 5, 10, 15, 20. Twenty minutes left! So it's TWENTY TO the next hour — not 40 past. Nobody says 40 past! And when the hand is on the 9, there are 15 minutes left — we call that QUARTER TO. Say the rule with me: past the 6, count what's LEFT, say '___ to'.
script.adaptHints: Sweep slowly and count the 5s with the child. If they love countdowns (rockets, races), frame it as 'the countdown side of the clock'.

plan.goal: Shared read: the child counts the minutes left for the hand on the 9 (quarter to) and then the 10 (10 to).
plan.note: The character draws, the child counts. Push for the words 'quarter to', not just '15'.
plan.successCriteria: Child counts 9→12 as 5, 10, 15 and says 'quarter to'; then reads the hand on the 10 as '10 to'.

script.say: Your turn to count! The minute hand is on the 9. Start at the 9 and count up to the 12 with me — 5, 10, 15. Fifteen minutes left! And what's the special name for 15 minutes to? … Quarter to! Now I'll sneak the hand up to the 10. Count what's left… so what time is it now?
script.adaptHints: Pause after each question. If the child says '15 to', celebrate it AND give the special name: 'quarter to'.

blocks.text: Minute hand on the 9: from the 9 up to the 12 is ___ minutes — quarter to!

check.question: Minute hand on the 9 — say the time as '___ to'.

wrongAnswers.why: right words, wrong side — hasn't switched at half past
wrongAnswers.remedy: Which side of the dashed line is the hand on? The left side counts what's LEFT — so is it past or to?

wrongAnswers.why: kept counting up past the 6
wrongAnswers.remedy: After half past we count DOWN. Start at the 9 and count up to the 12: 5, 10, 15 — fifteen left, so fifteen…?

plan.goal: Diagnose the core skill: hand on the 8 read as '20 to', not '40 past' — and name the correct next hour.
plan.note: This is the lesson's key diagnostic. '40 past' means the half-past switch hasn't landed; re-run the count-what's-left move on the marked clock.
plan.successCriteria: Child answers '20 to' and can say how many minutes are left to the top.

script.say: Check time! The minute hand is on the 8, and the hour hand is creeping up towards the 6. Read the time as 'something to'. Think: how many minutes are LEFT to the top?
script.adaptHints: After a correct answer, probe: 'How did you know it wasn't 40 past?' Then stretch: 'Which hour are we counting to — 5 or 6?'

blocks.prompt: The minute hand is on the 8. The time is…
blocks.explain: After half past we count what's LEFT: from the 8 up to the 12 is 5, 10, 15, 20 — twenty to. The hour hand is nearly at 6, so it's 20 to 6.

check.question: The minute hand is on the 8 — read the time as '___ to'.

wrongAnswers.why: still counting up past the 6 — the half-past switch hasn't happened
wrongAnswers.remedy: After half past we count what's LEFT. Start at the 8 and count up to the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20 — so twenty…?

wrongAnswers.why: read the number the hand points at instead of counting minutes
wrongAnswers.remedy: Each clock number is worth 5 minutes, remember? Count the gaps from the 8 up to the 12 in 5s.

wrongAnswers.why: named the hour the short hand just passed, not the one it's heading TO
wrongAnswers.remedy: Look at the short hand — it's nearly at the 6. Which hour are we counting down to?

plan.goal: Independent reading and setting of 'to' times; once secure, interleave past AND to faces so the child decides which word to use.
plan.note: Director draws from the practiceBank, start level 2. Watch for 'past' said on the left side and for miscounting the minutes left. The mixed past/to items are the level-3 goal.
plan.successCriteria: Child reads 3+ 'to' times correctly (including quarter to) and gets at least one mixed past/to decision right.

script.say: Practice time — you're the clock reader now! Some clocks, some tricks. And watch out: later I'll mix in a few from the PAST side, so you'll have to choose your word carefully.
script.adaptHints: Frame times around the child's day (swimming at quarter to 5, tea at 20 to 6) using their real routine or interests. Never change the clock maths.

stuckProtocol: Name why: 'I think we counted on the wrong side' or 'we counted the wrong way'.
Redraw the clock with the dashed middle line and shade the TO side green — count the left side together.
One hint: 'How far is it from the hand up to the 12?'
Re-ask with the hand on the 10 (the easiest 'to' — just 10 left), then build back to the 8.
Keep it safe: 'Mistakes show us what to practise. Smaller step.'

plan.goal: Child states the rule — when we say 'to' and what we count; end on an earned win.
plan.note: Child-led recall; the character listens, doesn't lecture.
plan.successCriteria: Child says something like 'after half past we count the minutes left to the next hour'.

script.say: Tell me the rule: when do we say 'to' instead of 'past'… and what exactly do we count? … Yes! After half past, we count the minutes LEFT until the next hour. You switched to counting down exactly at half past — that's the trickiest bit of clock reading, and you did it yourself.
script.adaptHints: Praise the specific process observed: counting up to the 12 in 5s, checking the hour hand, self-correcting a '40 past'.

block.prompt: The minute hand points at the 9. What do we say?
block.explain: From the 9 up to the 12 is 15 minutes — a quarter of the clock left. Quarter to!

wrongAnswers.why: right amount, wrong side of the clock
wrongAnswers.remedy: Is the hand on the left side or the right side? The left side counts what's LEFT — past or to?

wrongAnswers.why: read the clock number as the minutes
wrongAnswers.remedy: The 9 isn't 9 minutes — each number is worth 5. Count from the 9 up to the 12 in 5s.

hints: The hand is on the LEFT side — the 'to' side.
Count from the 9 up to the 12: 5, 10, 15.

reteach.say: Let's walk it: the hand is on the 9. From 9 to 10 is 5, to 11 is 10, to 12 is 15. Fifteen minutes left — and 15 to has a special name: QUARTER to.

block.definition: 15 minutes left before the next hour — minute hand on the 9

block.text: The minute hand is on the 10. From the 10 up to the 12 is ___ minutes.

wrongAnswers.why: counted the minutes gone by, not the minutes left
wrongAnswers.remedy: We only want what's LEFT. Count the jumps from the 10 up to the 12: 5… and one more jump?

wrongAnswers.why: counted the numbers, not the minutes
wrongAnswers.remedy: Each jump between numbers is worth 5 minutes. Two jumps of 5 make…?

hints: Each clock number is a jump of 5.
10 → 11 → 12: two jumps of 5.

reteach.say: Tiny count: from the 10, jump to the 11 — that's 5. Jump to the 12 — that's 10. Ten minutes left, so it's 10 to. The closer the hand gets to the top, the fewer minutes are left!

practiceBank.skill: say half past at the switch

block.prompt: The minute hand points straight down at the 6. What do we say?
block.explain: The 6 is halfway round — half past. One tick further and we switch to 'to'!

wrongAnswers.why: switched to 'to' too early — the 6 itself is still 'half past'
wrongAnswers.remedy: The 6 is exactly halfway — we say half past. The 'to' side starts once the hand moves PAST the 6.

wrongAnswers.why: read the clock number as the minutes
wrongAnswers.remedy: The 6 is worth 6 jumps of 5. Count in 5s round to the 6: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30.

hints: The 6 is exactly halfway round the clock.
Half of 60 minutes is 30 — half past.

reteach.say: The 6 is the halfway door. On the 6 we say HALF PAST. The moment the hand steps through that door, we start the countdown — 25 to, 20 to, quarter to… all the way to the next o'clock.

block.prompt: The minute hand points at the 8. The time is…
block.explain: From the 8 up to the 12: 5, 10, 15, 20 — twenty minutes left. 20 to!

wrongAnswers.why: kept counting up past the 6 — the classic trap
wrongAnswers.remedy: After half past we count what's LEFT, not what's gone. Count from the 8 up to the 12 in 5s.

wrongAnswers.why: counted the right amount but said the wrong side
wrongAnswers.remedy: Good counting — 20 is right! But the hand is on the LEFT side. Left side means minutes left, so twenty…?

hints: Which side of the clock is the 8 on?
Count from the 8 up to the 12: 5, 10, 15…

reteach.say: The 8 lives on the countdown side. Count what's left: 8 to 9 is 5, to 10 is 10, to 11 is 15, to 12 is 20. Twenty minutes to the next hour — 20 to. Nobody says 40 past!

block.prompt: You're setting the clock to 'twenty to 6'. Which number should the MINUTE hand point at?

wrongAnswers.why: counted 20 minutes on the PAST side instead of the TO side
wrongAnswers.remedy: The 4 gives 20 PAST. For 20 TO we need 20 minutes left — start at the 12 and count backwards in 5s: 11 is 5 to, 10 is 10 to…

wrongAnswers.why: looked for a '20' on the clock face
wrongAnswers.remedy: The clock only shows 1 to 12 — each number is worth 5 minutes. Which number leaves exactly 20 minutes to the top?

hints: Count backwards from the 12: 11 is 5 to, 10 is 10 to…
You need 4 jumps of 5 left to the top.

reteach.say: Walk backwards from the top: 11 means 5 to, 10 means 10 to, 9 means quarter to, 8 means 20 to. So 'twenty to' lives on the 8 — and the hour hand creeps close to the 6.

block.prompt: It's twenty to something. The HOUR hand is between the 5 and the 6, nearly touching the 6. What time is it?
block.explain: At 'to' times the hour hand is nearly at the NEXT hour. We're counting down TO 6 — so 20 to 6.

wrongAnswers.why: named the hour the hand already passed — the between-numbers trap
wrongAnswers.remedy: 5 o'clock is already finished — the hour hand left the 5 ages ago. Which number is it about to reach?

wrongAnswers.why: read the hour hand as if it had arrived
wrongAnswers.remedy: Nearly there, but not yet! The minute hand still has 20 minutes to go. So it's 20 minutes TO…?

hints: We count down TO the hour that's coming.
The hour hand is almost at the 6 — is 5 o'clock still coming, or already gone?

reteach.say: The hour hand tells a story: it left the 5 and it's nearly at the 6. So 5 o'clock is old news — the next hour is 6, and we're counting down to it. Twenty to SIX.

block.caption: The hour hand walks from 5 towards 6 — we name where it's GOING

block.prompt: Match the minute hand to the time we say.

wrongAnswers.why: counted the minutes gone by or muddled the countdown
wrongAnswers.remedy: For each one, count from the hand UP to the 12 in 5s — the 10 only has two jumps left.

hints: Count from each number up to the 12 in 5s.
The closer to the 12, the FEWER minutes left.

reteach.say: The countdown ladder: 8 is 20 to, 9 is quarter to, 10 is 10 to, 11 is 5 to. Every step towards the top means five fewer minutes left. Climb it with me: 20, 15, 10, 5!

block.prompt: Which side is the minute hand on? Sort each clock.

wrongAnswers.why: hasn't switched sides after half past
wrongAnswers.remedy: Picture the dashed line down the middle. Numbers 1 to 5 are the past side; 7 to 11 are the to side. Where does the 8 live?

hints: Draw the line from the 12 down to the 6 in your head.
Right side (1–5): past. Left side (7–11): to.

reteach.say: The clock is two countries: the right side is Past-land (1, 2, 3, 4, 5) and the left side is To-land (7, 8, 9, 10, 11). The minute hand's side picks the word — before you count anything, just ask: which country?

block.caption: Which country is the hand in?

block.statement: When the minute hand is on the 8, the time is '40 past'.
block.explain: After half past we count the minutes LEFT: from the 8 up to the 12 is 20 — so it's 20 to, not 40 past.

wrongAnswers.why: the lesson's core misconception — counting up past the 6
wrongAnswers.remedy: 40 minutes HAVE gone by — that's true — but clocks don't say it that way. What do we count once the hand passes the 6?

hints: What do we count after half past — minutes gone, or minutes left?
Count from the 8 up to the 12 in 5s.

reteach.say: Sneaky one! Forty minutes really have gone past — but after half past, clock language flips to the countdown. Twenty minutes are left, so we say 20 to. Same moment, better words.

block.caption: Minute hand on the 8: we say 20 to

block.prompt: A friend reads a clock with the minute hand on the 8 as '40 past 5'. What should they say instead — and what did they forget?
block.sample: They should say '20 to 6'. After half past you count the minutes LEFT to the next hour, and the next hour is 6.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: 20 to 6 — after half past we count the minutes left to the NEXT hour

wrongAnswers.why: swapped the word but kept counting up, and kept the old hour
wrongAnswers.remedy: Two fixes needed: count from the 8 UP to the 12 for the minutes left, and check which hour the short hand is heading to.

wrongAnswers.why: fixed the counting but named the hour that's already gone
wrongAnswers.remedy: Great counting — 20 is right! Now the hour: the short hand has left the 5 and is nearly at the 6. Which hour is coming?

hints: Fix the minutes first: count from the 8 up to the 12.
Then fix the hour: which number is the short hand heading TO?

reteach.say: Two-step fix: step one, after half past count what's LEFT — 8 up to 12 is 20. Step two, name the hour you're counting TO — the short hand is nearly at 6. Put them together: 20 to 6. That's the whole secret of the 'to' side.

steps: Hand past the 6? Switch to countdown.
Count from the hand up to the 12 in 5s.
Name the hour the short hand is heading TO.

adaptivity.levelUp: 2 consecutive correct at the current level → next level; at level 3, interleave past AND to faces so the child chooses the word each time.
adaptivity.levelDown: 2 misses on the same skill → run that item's reteach with the two-sided clock redrawn (dashed middle line, TO side shaded), then serve a level-1 item of the same skill.
adaptivity.masterySignal: 3+ correct across levels 2–3 including one 'set the clock' item, one next-hour item and one mixed past/to decision → mastery ≥ 0.8 for 'minutes to the hour'.
struggleProtocol: Name why: wrong half of the clock, or counting the wrong direction.
Redraw the clock with the middle line marked and count the left side together in 5s.
One hint: 'How far from the hand up to the 12?'
Re-ask with the hand on the 10 (only 10 left), then build back to the 8.
Keep it safe: 'Mistakes show us what to practise — smaller step.'
adaptivity.personalization: Anchor 'to' times in the child's real day (LearnerModel.interests and routine): 'swimming at quarter to 5', 'tea at 20 to 6'. Never change the clock maths.
adaptivity.endOnSuccess: Finish on a winnable clock (hand on the 10 or 9 if needed), then specific process praise: 'you counted what was LEFT — that's the exact switch that trips most people up.'

differentiation.support: Keep the past/to halves marked with the dashed line; always count the minutes remaining out loud together; stay on the 9 and 10 until secure.
differentiation.stretch: Read a random mix of past and to faces with no middle line drawn; link times to a daily timetable ('what are you doing at quarter to 5?').

extension: 'What's the time?' race — the character sets a time, the child reads it; then the child calls a 'to' time and the character has to say which number the minute hand points at (and sometimes gets it cheekily wrong for the child to catch).
assessmentEvidence: Child reads 'minutes to' times to 5 minutes including quarter to, sets 'twenty to 6', and chooses past vs to correctly on a mixed face.
revisitLater: Mixed past/to clock reading returns as a starter in Unit 8; the end-of-unit-6 check (quarter past, quarter to, 10 past 4, set twenty to 6) runs at the start of Lesson 21.
